Sweeps

A sweep runs the sheet once for each value of one input, or for each combination of the values of two, and collects chosen results from every run. The sixth example, Help › Examples › Sweeps, runs the Rankine cycle of the third example for turbine inlet temperatures from 400 °C to 600 °C. It opens in the Sweep view and runs.

The sweep lines

The sweep is written in its own editor in the Sweep view; the sheet stays as it is.

sweep T_1 = 400:20:600 [C]
record eta, x_2, w_net, bwr
plot eta vs T_1
plot x_2 vs T_1
  • sweep names the input and its values: start:step:stop, or a list such as 5, 7, 9. The swept variable must be an input of the sheet: an input is a line name = number [unit], or a number written in a state line (x = 0 in state 3 makes x_3 an input).
  • record lists the variables kept from each run, for the table.
  • plot draws one chart per line: plot eta vs T_1, or several variables on one chart: plot eta, x_2 vs T_1.

Run, in the header, runs the sweep again after an edit (⌘Enter, or CtrlEnter on Windows and Linux).

Families of curves

A second sweep line runs the sheet for every combination of the two swept variables. Each plot line is drawn against one of them, with one curve for each value of the other. For the cold air-standard Otto cycle, whose thermal efficiency is eta = 1 - r^(1 - k):

sweep r = 2:1:12
sweep k = 1.3, 1.35, 1.4
plot eta vs r

draws three curves of eta against r, one for each k, with a legend reading k = 1.3, k = 1.35 and k = 1.4; plot eta vs k draws one curve for each r instead. Each value of k has its own color and marker shape, the same in every plot, and its own line style; in a plot of several variables, such as plot eta, x_2 vs r, the line style tells the variables apart instead. The curves can be told apart in a printed copy. A plot against a variable that is not swept is refused, and a sweep of more than 2000 runs is refused with the number of runs. The results table has a row for each run, with both swept variables as columns, grouped by the value of the variable that makes the curves of the first plot. A run that fails leaves a gap in its curve and is listed under the sweep editor; a click on a listed run moves the sliders to it.

The slider

The slider under the chart steps through the runs, and every pane follows it: the sheet's values, the Workspace, the states table and the figures show the run the slider is on. A click on a row of the results table moves the slider to that run. With two sweep lines there is a slider for each swept variable: moving one keeps the other at its value, so the run moves along one curve, and the run the sliders are on is drawn as filled markers. Any pane of the Sweep view can show a figure of the sheet through its pane menu; below, the slider is at the last run and the lower pane shows the T–s diagram of that run.

Leaving the Sweep view returns every pane to the sheet as written.

Exporting a sweep

The export button of a sweep chart writes it as PNG, SVG or PDF, copies it as an image, copies its data as tab-separated text, or writes the data as CSV or a MATLAB script. With two sweep lines the CSV has one row per run, and the MATLAB script writes each recorded variable as a matrix, a row for each value of the first swept variable and a column for each value of the second, with one plot call per curve. A sweep that has run can also be included in a published report (see Publishing and exporting).
